title: The Altar of Witness
reflectionText: A great altar stood beside the Jordan, visible enough to summon an army and yet built for a purpose the distant tribes had not heard. The eastern tribes called it a witness for generations, not a place of sacrifice. What is it to let a careful defense name the purpose of a troubling sign?
editorialNotes: Packet 016 writer output. Short-only owner plan. The retelling presents the altar as the eastern tribes’ witness rather than a rival sacrificial altar and ends with their defense in Joshua 22:29, without importing verses 30-34.
